relevance_note: This is a single-centre retrospective review of anakinra use in 47 patients with SJIA, CAPS, MKD, SURF, PIMS-TS and other inflammatory conditions ("Other AID, Blau syndrome and Pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum and acne syndrome"); it never mentions TNFAIP3, A20 or A20 haploinsufficiency, so no individual with a TNFAIP3 variant is reported.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no script transcribed any table. A case-insensitive text search for 'TNFAIP3', 'A20', 'HA20' and 'haploinsuff' found only the DOI fragment 'NEJMoa2021680' in the reference list, so the paper reports no TNFAIP3 carriers. Only the publications row is filled, and the other four tables are empty, as the instructions require for papers without TNFAIP3 individuals. n_patients_reported is null rather than 0 because the authors never state a count of TNFAIP3-variant patients; the cohort overall has 47 patients ('From 47 patients (27 female patients) who fulfilled inclusion criteria'). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null: the CAPS paragraph cites reference 30 (a Muckle-Wells family report by the same group) after 'Two patients required dose escalation (to 200 mg/day) in order to maintain disease inactivity (30)', but the paper does not explicitly state that these patients were described earlier, and they are not TNFAIP3 patients. No internal contradictions were relevant to HA20.

span: Electronic hospital records were reviewed retrospectively.
From 47 patients (27 female patients) who fulfilled inclusion criteria
